task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a reported feature of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about residents taking part in Mossgate's neighborhood drain-observation program. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Mossgate drain-observation program asks registered residents to watch designated street drain openings and report problems to the works office.
The program permits removal of loose surface leaves from a safe public position under its guidance, not opening grates or entering drains.
Resident Tera Noll checks the drain near her usual walking route after leaves fall from the trees along the curb.
The supplied scene describes Noll placing loose leaves into a bag and photographing the cleared surface to accompany her report.
A clear surface opening does not establish that the underground pipe is clear or that nearby properties cannot flood.
Noll said, "I know this corner because I pass it all the time. The program gave me somewhere to send what I was noticing."
The city remains responsible for underground maintenance and sends trained crews when a report indicates work beyond the volunteer role.
The program is not a transfer of the city's drainage duties to private residents.
Works supervisor Elrin Voss said, "A useful report can get the right crew to the right place. It does not ask a neighbor to become that crew."
Participants are told not to work during dangerous conditions or from the traffic lane to complete a check.
Reports use the city's location references so staff can distinguish neighboring openings that look similar in a close photograph.
The office acknowledges a report and records its status; acknowledgment is not a statement that a repair has already been completed.
Residents may participate by observing and reporting even if they cannot remove leaves themselves.
The city provides collection bags and a short orientation at the community center.
The program's first season has produced a record of reports, but the packet contains no measured reduction in flooding or maintenance costs.
The works office compares reports with its routine inspection schedule rather than rely only on locations with an active volunteer.
A drain without a registered observer remains part of the city's maintenance responsibility.
Some participants have given their adopted locations informal names, while official work orders continue to use the city's identifiers.
Noll's route includes a stop at a neighborhood shop, making the check part of an ordinary trip rather than a separate patrol of the whole district.
The city will review whether report descriptions give crews enough information before expanding the program.
The program page is not an emergency-warning service and does not replace the city's urgent reporting channels.
No live storm conditions or actual private property addresses are supplied in the case.

forbidden_additions: Public entry into drains or work in dangerous conditions.
A clear opening treated as proof of flood protection.
Transferred city duties, completed repairs inferred from acknowledgments or measured program savings.
preserve: The resident's ordinary observation routine and the limited volunteer role.
The connection between a useful report and professional maintenance responsibility.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
